text: The device hums. A dry wilderness of rock and brush, with a great mountain rising at the edge of the sky. A shepherd stands with his flock in the heat.
Forty years have passed since the baby was found in the river. Moses grew up in the palace, ran away to Midian, married, and has lived as a shepherd ever since.

speaker: Moses
text: A shepherd's life is a quiet one. I had a different one once, in Egypt.

speaker: Moses
text: {name}? Welcome. It is not often that I have company out here. I am Moses.
Meanwhile, Moses was shepherding the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.

speaker: Moses
text: Some of the sheep have strayed. Will you help me bring them back before we move on?
The sheep are not lost yet.
You walk the stray sheep back to the flock. It trots along happily.

speaker: Moses
text: All of them. Thank you, {name}. Come. I want to take the flock to the mountain, to the far side of the wilderness.
There the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a blazing fire from within a bush. Moses saw the bush ablaze with fire, but it was not consumed.

speaker: Moses
text: I must go over and see this marvelous sight. Why is the bush not burning up?
When the LORD saw that he had gone over to look, God called out to him from within the bush, “Moses, Moses!” “Here I am,” he answered.
“Do not come any closer,” God said. “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.”
God told Moses to take off his sandals. The ground was holy because God was there. This is the first time the Bible calls a place holy.
Then He said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” At this, Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.

speaker: The LORD
text: I have indeed seen the affliction of My people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out because of their oppressors, and I am aware of their sufferings.

speaker: The LORD
text: I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land to a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey …

speaker: The LORD
text: Therefore, go! I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.

speaker: Moses
text: Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of Egypt?

speaker: The LORD
text: I will surely be with you, | and this will be the sign to you that I have sent you: When you have brought the people out of Egypt, all of you will worship God on this mountain.
Moses was afraid and said he was not good enough. God did not say that he was. God said, "I will be with you." That was all Moses needed.

speaker: Moses
text: Suppose I go to the Israelites and say to them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you,’ and they ask me, ‘What is His name?’ What should I tell them?

speaker: God
text: I AM WHO I AM. This is what you are to say to the Israelites: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’

speaker: God
text: Say to the Israelites, ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered in every generation.
Long after, Jesus used the same words about Himself:

speaker: Jesus
text: Truly, truly, I tell you, | before Abraham was born, I am!

speaker: Moses
text: What if they do not believe me or listen to my voice? For they may say, ‘The LORD has not appeared to you.’

speaker: The LORD
text: What is that in your hand?

speaker: Moses
text: A staff,
“Throw it on the ground,” said the LORD. So Moses threw it on the ground, and it became a snake, and he ran from it.
“Stretch out your hand and grab it by the tail,” the LORD said to Moses, who reached out his hand and caught the snake, and it turned back into a staff in his hand.

speaker: Moses
text: Please, Lord, | I have never been eloquent, neither in the past nor since You have spoken to Your servant, for I am slow of speech and tongue.

speaker: The LORD
text: Who gave man his mouth? Or who makes the mute or the deaf, the sighted or the blind? Is it not I, the LORD? Now go! I will help you as you speak, and I will teach you what to say.

speaker: Moses
text: Please, Lord, send someone else.

speaker: The LORD
text: Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well, and he is now on his way to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.
Moses said, "Send someone else." God was patient with him, and sent his brother Aaron to help. God often sends help to people who are afraid.

speaker: Aaron
text: I had a dream telling me to come. And here you are, after forty years!
Meanwhile, the LORD had said to Aaron, “Go and meet Moses in the wilderness.” So he went and met Moses at the mountain of God and kissed him.
And Moses told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say, and all the signs He had commanded him to perform.
Then Moses and Aaron went and assembled all the elders of the Israelites, and Aaron relayed everything the LORD had said to Moses. And Moses performed the signs before the people, and they believed.
And when they heard that the LORD had attended to the Israelites and had seen their affliction, they bowed down and worshiped.

speaker: Moses
text: {name}, I will go back to Egypt. I am frightened. But He said He will be with me. That is enough.
Your device hums. Time to go.

speaker: Zipporah
text: My husband is a quiet man. He was a prince in Egypt once, you know. Now he walks behind sheep. But he is happy here.
Moses agreed to stay with the man, and he gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage.
Long after, the letter to the Hebrews said why Moses left the palace:
By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter. He chose to suffer oppression with God’s people rather than to experience the fleeting enjoyment of sin.

speaker: Elder
text: We have prayed for rescue for years. And now Moses is here with signs, saying that God has seen us. We believe!
… they bowed down and worshiped.
The glowing door nearby leads back to your time device.
